meta.description: Lightning Jar is a design and build technology studio handcrafting websites, web applications and custom AI applications for businesses and organizations.
meta.title: Lightning Jar

topics.heading: Design & Build Technology Studio
text: For twenty-five years, we've been too busy designing and building websites, web applications, and custom software to put the proper time and attention into our own damn marketing. That's not just an excuse. It is also a point of pride.

Now the ground is moving again. We're in a new era defined by large language models, the largest shift we've seen since the web itself. Our answer is the same as it has always been: build, don't wait. Today that means leading with open research and practical guidance for developers of LLM applications.

primary.label: Read Our Story
primary.title: If the Solution Is Not Beautiful, It Is Wrong: Twenty-Five Years of Lightning Jar

topics.heading: Digital From the Beginning
text: We started planning the business in late 2001 and launched our first website, just a splash page then, before the year was out. By 2002 we were operating in earnest, the same year the "digital information age" was said to have officially begun, when the total amount of digitized information in the world exceeded traditional analog information.

primary.title: If the Solution Is Not Beautiful, It Is Wrong: Twenty-Five Years of Lightning Jar

topics.heading: Skeptical of Easy Answers
text: We believe great strategy is the process of asking tough questions. Great design is the process of making tough decisions. Great implementation is the process of making tough compromises.

topics.heading: We Love Open Source Software
text: Open source is an open, collaborative, and community-driven approach to software development. It promotes transparency, innovation, and cost-effectiveness. Whatever your technology challenge, there is probably an open-source solution that is the best choice to solve it.

primary.label: Why Open Source Wins
primary.title: Why Open Source Beats Proprietary Platforms for B2B Websites

topics.heading: We Believe in Research
text: Good engineering decisions come from evidence, not vibes. That's why we run and publish open-source research for developers of LLM applications: a growing series of pre-registered studies, more than 13,000 scored model runs and counting, corrections included.

secondary.label: Latest Findings
secondary.title: The Thirty-Sixth Edit: Long LLM Sessions Don't Need Memory Either

topics.heading: Fact vs. Fiction in the Age of LLMs
text: It has never been easier for a business to get swept up in AI hype, and never harder to tell the real opportunities from the noise. We help businesses adapt their marketing technology and sales tools to the LLM era with a customized, research-driven approach: test the claims, filter out the fiction, and invest only in what the evidence supports.

secondary.label: SEO In The Age of LLMs
secondary.title: SEO In The Age of LLMs

topics.heading: Saying No is a Superpower
text: It took us a long time to learn how to say no. Now we say it all the time. We don't take on all clients or project requests. We only take the ones that are a good fit for our team, our availability, and our working culture, when the timeline and goals are realistic, and when we are certain we can deliver real value.

ticker: We were going to put an image on this page.
It was going to be really nice.
But we never got around to it.
We couldn't decide if it should be puppies with kittens or robots with lasers.
Then we thought maybe it should be puppies with lasers.
Or kittens with robots?
We couldn't decide.
So this is what we ended up with.
Kind of disappointing, right?
Well, it is what it is.
Not to ruin the surprise, but...
Nothing special happens if you keep clicking.
Seriously.
Not a thing.
Nada.
Nothing.
Zip.
Zero.
Zilch.
Although...
At some point it will probably explode.
Just kidding.
It is not going to explode.
Probably.
At some point it will just loop back to the beginning.
So, you should probably just go back to work.
But, that doesn't sound very appealing does it?
At least you won't be stuck here clicking this button anymore.
Seriously, you should go for a walk.
Touch some grass or something.
Maybe take an early lunch.
Maybe pay attention to that Zoom call you're on.
You must have SOMETHING better to do.
A TPS report or something?
BTW, remember when most of the internet was like this?
Little silly surprises... people who were in it for a laugh more than a buck?
That was a long time ago, wasn't it?
Sigh...
The internet is just kind of terrible today isn't it?
I mean, it doesn't have to be, but it is.
And it isn't getting better anytime soon, what with AI everything, all the time.
It is something to think about.
Especially if you are in charge of a website-- which, unfortunately for both of us, I am.
The way I see it, there are two paths:
You can design a generic, corporate-looking website.
Fill it with bland AI-generated copy and some AI-generated stock photos.
Cram it to the brim with invasive third-party tracking scripts.
Maybe throw in some press clippings for the investors.
And call it a day.
OR... and this might sound crazy...
You could actually try to make something that is both beautiful and functional.
Or, at least, useful for your clients.
Maybe something that makes sense and answers some real questions.
Maybe even tells an interesting story.
Just saying-- it's worth a thought.
I see lots of companies wasting their time on social media.
Let me tell you: no one in all of social media cares about interacting with your company unless it is to complain.
Other companies blow a lot of budget on videos that, metrics prove, no one will ever watch.
Sometimes all of the money goes to digital ads.
And the grim truth is, they mostly don't work.
Unless your goal is to spend an insane amount of money very quickly.
And you're not even sure if it's working, because you're not sure what you're measuring.
I mean, all of that is very easy to do, and you won't stand out if you do it.
But, maybe there is a better way.
I'm not saying an easier way, mind you.
But a better way.
To carefully design, build, and manage your marketing websites, web tools, and web applications.
So they work.
They look nice.
They are easy to use and don't drive your customers bonkers.
Maybe they even say real things in plain language.
Maybe they include tools that solve real problems for you, your partners, or your customers.
Maybe users keeping coming back.
Not because you chase them with digital ads all over the internet.
But because you respect your users, and you are providing something of real value.
Or you made them smile.
Or you made them click {{count}} times on one single button
And they didn't hate it.
